general: Retain all 126 race-by-culture-by-role combinations. No listed ancestry needs exclusion from a culture, learned profession or sacred role.
Describe the collection as fantasy characters in historically informed dress, adapted to miniature production constraints; do not claim exact historical reconstruction.
Use the same house anatomy, adult character treatment, clothing quality and range of expressions in every culture. Do not add racial caricature to facial features.

Distribute permitted skin colours within each ancestry across all packs without linking darkness, redness or greenness to evil, primitiveness, caste or social rank. No culture-specific whitening or de-horning is needed.

Religious practitioners may be sincere members of their traditions regardless of fantasy ancestry. Do not equate tieflings with local demons, dragonborn with local deities, or orcs with historical ethnic groups.
Keep the no-blue/teal/cyan, no-writing/symbols, solid-parts, still-pose and low-rogue-blade constraints. State once in catalogue context that colours and fine details are simplified.
Closed books may have hidden contents. Blank astrolabes, compasses and divining boards are visual miniatures, not accurate functional instruments; do not invent substitute pseudo-script.
Keep women in all roles. Distinguish intentional fantasy access to occupations and dress from claims about historical prevalence.
Caster is a game category, not a claim that historical physicians, scholars or members of a religion wielded supernatural powers.

Review finished figures at table distance and as isolated catalogue thumbnails. This review assesses descriptions, not unseen meshes. Targeted feedback from relevant practitioners, historians and Nahua reviewers would improve release confidence.

changes.where: ALL, ancestry descriptions and game metadata
changes.issue: A complete visual grid does not counteract rules or descriptions that still define orcs as savage or tieflings as inherently evil.
changes.change_to: Ancestry does not determine morality, intelligence, civilisation, religious sincerity or fitness for office. Describe these as individual characters; do not attach savage, primitive, corrupt or evil tags by ancestry.

changes.where: ALL, helmets, hats, robes and non-human anatomy
changes.issue: Unadapted clothing can turn horns, ears, tails and muzzles into costume jokes or impossible fittings.
changes.change_to: Tailor garments and headgear to each body while preserving the historical silhouette. Use reinforced horn openings, fitted muzzle clearances and discreet tail openings. Keep horns anatomically distinct from helmet ornament, tails close to the body, and feet securely supported.

changes.where: IND, pack names and search aliases
changes.issue: Hindu-tiefling-warrior assigns a religion from regional clothing and encourages a demon-versus-religion reading.
changes.change_to: Use Rajasthani tiefling spear warrior, with Jaipur–Amber, 18th century in the pack description. Do not use Hindu as a synonym for Indian or Rajasthani. Reserve religious identification for an explicitly characterised individual.

changes.issue: Palm-leaf manuscripts are not impossible, but they are a less well-targeted default for this eighteenth-century north Indian court than paper manuscripts.
changes.change_to: Both hands hold a closed rectangular bundle of paper manuscript folios between plain dark covers, tied with a cord, against the chest. No writing is visible.

changes.issue: Wooden sandals on every court scholar, physician and astrologer add an unnecessary ascetic association.
changes.change_to: Replace wooden sandals with plain soft leather slippers or modest leather shoes. Retain the cream jama, folded shawl and head covering.

changes.issue: Replacing only the hat leaves the physician in the onmyoji's formal ceremonial ensemble.
changes.change_to: In plain late-Edo professional dress: a charcoal kosode secured with an obi, a plain brown haori without crests, white tabi and straw sandals; no eboshi or diviner's ceremonial trousers. Both hands support the existing compact medicine chest.

changes.issue: A wakizashi is a short sword rather than the compact knife required by the stated rogue silhouette.
changes.change_to: The RIGHT hand holds a short plain tanto point-down close beside the thigh; the LEFT hand holds the existing compact coil of ochre rope.

changes.issue: Two different weapon kits share the same identifier, making the figure assignments ambiguous.
changes.change_to: Use samurai-yari and samurai-katana as distinct kit identifiers. Display names may be samurai spear warrior and samurai swordsman. Assign each listed samurai explicitly to one kit.

changes.where: CHN, herbal physician and geomancer dress
changes.issue: The shared dress makes every physician and geomancer a Daoist ritual specialist without establishing that identity.
changes.change_to: For physician and geomancer: a plain long charcoal or brown robe with a right-side fastening, cream trousers, black cloth shoes and a modest dark cap. Retain their respective medicine box and simplified compass. Reserve explicitly Daoist dress for the Daoist priest kit.

changes.issue: A symbol-free plain robe should not be described as a complete formal liturgical vestment.
changes.change_to: A Daoist ritual specialist in a plain everyday robe, holding simplified ritual implements. Keep the peach-wood sword and bell, with no inscriptions or symbols; do not claim reproduction of a particular ordination rank or full ceremonial vestment.

changes.where: CHN, dwarf and tiefling night runner
changes.issue: The familiar butterfly-sword form is more securely associated with nineteenth-century southern Chinese evidence than Beijing around 1770.
changes.change_to: The RIGHT hand holds one short plain single-edged knife point-down close beside the thigh; the LEFT hand holds the existing rope coil. Do not use paired butterfly swords or modern folding butterfly knives.

changes.where: CHN, halfling and dragonborn wandering swordsman
changes.issue: The upright full-length jian contradicts the explicit short, low-held rogue blade requirement.
changes.change_to: Rename the kit wandering scout. The RIGHT hand holds a short plain straight knife point-down beside the thigh; the LEFT hand holds a compact cloth travel bundle against the waist. Retain the working clothes.

changes.issue: The jian-and-shield pairing is a less convincing default military combination than a dao with the shield.
changes.change_to: The RIGHT hand holds a curved single-edged DAO sabre upright beside the shoulder; the LEFT arm holds the existing plain ochre rattan shield. Give this kit a distinct identifier, bannerman-shield.

changes.issue: Unspecified hair invites generic ancient-China topknots and ignores the Qing anchor.
changes.change_to: Where historically conventional lay male hair is visible, use the Qing shaved-front-and-queue arrangement, with the braid resting against the back. Treat religious hairstyles separately. Where fixed house hair cannot be changed, use the existing appropriate cap, headcloth or helmet rather than inventing a generic topknot.

changes.issue: One gown-and-beads ensemble is presented as universal dress for seers, healers and poets.
changes.change_to: Provide two plain clothing variants: the existing long gown ensemble, and a burgundy wool tunic over cream linen with wool trousers, belt and short cloak. Choose deliberately for each character; do not treat either outfit as an occupational uniform or forbid characters from crossing historical gender conventions.

changes.where: MDE, pack description and civilian names
changes.issue: Mamluk can denote a military status as well as the sultanate; not every inhabitant was a mamluk soldier.
changes.change_to: Pack title: Mamluk-era Cairo and Damascus, 14th century. Civilian descriptions should say a physician, scholar, scout or other resident of that setting, without assigning mamluk military status. Existing short catalogue names may remain under this pack heading.

changes.where: MES, women in rogue and caster civilian dress
changes.issue: The universal loincloth-and-mantle template erases a distinctive local women's clothing tradition and may produce unnecessarily exposed caricatures.
changes.change_to: Use a plain cream rectangular huipilli blouse over a calf- or ankle-length wrapped cueitl skirt secured with a woven sash, with plain burgundy edging where appropriate. A short travel mantle may be added close to the body. Keep role props unchanged. Retain the armoured fighter outfits.

changes.where: MES, orc and elf jaguar warrior; dwarf and tiefling eagle warrior
changes.issue: Animal suits on non-human bodies can be rendered as feral anatomy, trophy skins or comic animal costumes.
changes.change_to: Render both suits as carefully fitted, manufactured military garments with smooth close-laid featherwork. Keep the wearer's house face clearly distinct inside a constructed animal-head helmet. Do not add blood, torn hides, extra fangs, skull trophies or an animalistic crouch. Adapt the tiefling's helmet around its existing horns.

changes.issue: A generic wooden backpack frame can drift into a European expedition-pack silhouette.
changes.change_to: Show a compact wrapped trade load supported by broad carrying straps, including a load-bearing forehead strap resting securely against the head where anatomy permits. Keep any frame mostly concealed and all straps in solid contact with the figure.

keep_as_is: Every ancestry appearing in every culture and all three broad roles.
Rajasthani tiefling spear warrior, Mexica orc jaguar warrior and Chinese tiefling Daoist priest as catalogue names.
Orc scholars, physicians, skalds, elders and painter-scribes; tiefling astrologers, onmyoji, seers and day-count readers.
Dragonborn scholars or ritual specialists without equating their anatomy with a local dragon deity.
IND: studded padded armour, talwar, dhal, barchha, gurz and katar as historically informed kit choices; the Jaipur astrolabe is especially apt.
JPN: Edo armour, yari, naginata, katana, visible faces and non-ninja working clothes; onmyoji retained for the Edo anchor.
CHN: cloth-covered riveted armour as a simplified Qing form, dao, qiang and the tightly bound red tassel.
NRS: mail, round shields, spears, axes, swords and unornamented helmets; a simplified basket-terminal staff is a defensible seer attribute.
MDE: lamellar over mail, straight swords, maces, turbans, hospital physician, astrologer and alchemist.
RUS: Rus' terminology, Kyiv spelling, retinue armour, teardrop shields, practical healers and restrained civilian dress.
MES: cotton armour, crafted featherwork war suits, macuahuitl, tepoztopilli, chimalli, cacao, closed screenfold books, ticitl and tlacuilo roles.
Low-held plain rogue blades, including obsidian blades in MES, without blood or sacrificial staging.
Varied permitted skin colours, intact house horns and tails, and equal armour coverage for women.
